subject.title: [Feature]: Inline agent widgets in web chat via client-capability-gated tools

question: Should OpenClaw add a client-capability-gated tool contract and a Canvas-owned `show_widget` tool for sandboxed web chat widgets, or keep this outside core/plugin SDK for now?
rationale: The requested feature changes model-visible tool availability and renders agent-authored markup, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent trust, sandbox, plugin API, and product boundary.

options.title: Approve Canvas-hosted widget seam
options.body: Add `inline-widgets` as an additive client capability, thread per-run client caps into tool assembly, expose a narrow `requiredClientCaps` tool contract, and implement `show_widget` inside Canvas with CSP, sandbox, cleanup, and tests.

options.title: Keep widget plugin-only for now
options.body: Decline the core capability seam until an external ClawHub/plugin prototype proves that existing plugin APIs are insufficient.

options.title: Defer to broader client metadata design
options.body: Wait for the WebChat client-type/trust contract to settle before using client-declared data for model-visible tool selection.

recommendation.title: Approve Canvas-hosted widget seam
recommendation.body: Add `inline-widgets` as an additive client capability, thread per-run client caps into tool assembly, expose a narrow `requiredClientCaps` tool contract, and implement `show_widget` inside Canvas with CSP, sandbox, cleanup, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/security boundary decision spanning Gateway protocol, plugin SDK, Canvas, and WebChat behavior.
